references.text: Moses commands the Israelites to explain to their children the meaning of the Passover celebration, just as Joshua commands them to tell their children about the crossing of the Jordan.
The command to tell children about God's mighty acts at the Exodus from Egypt, paralleled with the command to tell them about the crossing of the Jordan.
The instruction to explain to the sons the meaning of the Lord's mighty acts, corresponding to the account of the crossing of the Jordan.
Israel's crossing through the Red Sea on dry ground, which serves as a type for the crossing of the Jordan on dry land.
Moses' command to tell children about the Exodus from Egypt and God's deeds, paralleled with Joshua's command regarding the crossing of the Jordan.
The earlier instruction in the same chapter to tell children the meaning of the memorial stones from the Jordan.
The psalmist recalls how God turned the sea into dry land and the people crossed the river on foot.
The poetry celebrates how the sea fled and the Jordan turned back, a poetic retelling of Israel's crossing.
